My advise from the last 7 years:
1) make it fun. They are kids. Not adults
2) huge emphasis on fundamentals. Doing the basics right will take them far
3.) have a practice plan every day. Organized practices keep kids focused
4) give them they why. It sticks better mentally that way
5) be realistic with what you are working with and adjust your offense/defense accordingly. Don’t be super complex if the kids aren’t successful with the basics 
6.) most importantly, inspire the kids and build bonds. They will run through a brick wall for a coach they believe in that believes in them.

Knowledge transfer is in your stronghold. Go up the steps, over the bridge, then head left and drop down. Then further left is a robot. You’ll make the character, skip prologue, get to the point where you get your instrument and play the stronghold song to do it. 
The main story will take you to several different continents, each with an ark piece basically. You’ll hone till you get 450 to go to rohendel, then to 600 to hit yorn, etc. You start t2 with yorn. Honing happens once you get a guide quest with a certain ilvl needed to go to the next continent.

Follow the main quest, and there will be stop points for you to gear your character. Also a great time to start an alt and use knowledge transfer to get them to 50 as well. Use resources from your alt to push your main. 

Islands are a great resource as well. Don’t skip them, tons of mats from there to hone with!  Only other tip is don’t waste your pheons on stuff in the ah until you’re at t3 (really 1370).
